ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set g_x = 0 for all items so kappa_x = 0 everywhere; the residual transport becomes u_{l+1} = u_l, i.e. plain curvature-c RQ with Poincare assignment. The switch exists in code (behaviour_weight = 0 or an empty successor table) and is exercised by a unit test, but no arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: curvature c = 1 Poincare assignment and transport plus the successor-direction damping with the measured kappa_x. This is the one and only trained candidate.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp_0^c, log_0^c and d_c by the identity and the Euclidean distance (the c -> 0 limit), keep the same kappa_x damping in flat space and the Euclidean codebook update. The switch exists in code (curvature = 0 / euclidean_geometry = True) and is exercised by a unit test, but no arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the Stage-2 TRAINING split sequences, grouped by user, in time order. For every occurrence of item x, the following H = 3 positions in the same user's sequence contribute one count to each successor item s (self-transitions dropped); counts are summed over all users and occurrences. S_x is the top-20 successors by count; g_x = sum_{s in S_x} count(x,s) * log_0^c(E_s) / sum count(x,s), where E_s is the item embedding under the frozen pretraining encoder snapshot. g_x is stored as a d-vector plus its count; the table is refreshed once at epoch 1500 from the current encoder (fixed schedule). Only training-split sequences are read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed successor direction g_x of each training item, built from training-split sequences only (top-20 successors by count over the next H = 3 positions in the same user's sequence), used as a per-item direction in the tangent space at the origin.
ideas.cost_estimate: No new forward passes and no new parameters. Added per step at the frozen scale: batch is ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items, 3 levels x 1023 x 256 Poincare distances (~0.8M artanh per step, ~40 MFLOP), plus three log/exp maps and one 3-term projection per item; roughly 5-10% over the baseline SID-training step, i.e. minutes over the 3000-epoch (72000-step) Stage-2 run. The successor table is one offline pass over the training split (counting top-20 successors per item, minutes on CPU) and is refreshed once at the fixed epoch 1500 using the current encoder (a documented schedule, not a tuned constant).
ideas.coupling_equation: u_{l+1} = (1 - kappa_x) u_l + kappa_x <u_l, g_hat_x> g_hat_x, with u_l = log_0^c(z_l) - log_0^c(e_{l,k_l}) and kappa_x = |<u_l, g_hat_x>| / (||u_l|| ||g_hat_x||); equivalently u_{l+1} = u_parallel + (1 - kappa_x) u_perp where u_parallel = <u_l, g_hat_x> g_hat_x is the training-successor component and log_0^c / exp_0^c with curvature c carry the geometry. k_l = argmin_k (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-z_l) (+) e_{l,k}||).
ideas.coupling_path: One chain: curved log-map of the item -> curved residual at level l -> measurement of the angle between that residual and the behaviour direction g_x -> kappa_x sets the anisotropy of that same residual -> curved exp-map produces the level-(l+1) input -> level-(l+1) curved assignment -> SID token. Removing the behaviour makes kappa_x = 0 and the chain collapses to plain curved RQ; removing curvature replaces log/exp/d_c by identity/Euclidean maps so the residual and the assignment change for every item past level 1. Neither term can be deleted without changing the actual quantizer input and therefore the SID assignment.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Damping the behaviour-contradicting part of the inter-level residual makes deep prefixes transferable, so on the single frozen run the history-conditioned hit rate of the level-2/3 code should exceed that of the plain curved quantizer, per-level assignment entropy should drop, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065; if the deep-prefix hit rate stays flat and recall stays at baseline, the mechanism is not worth keeping.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantizer, on two things at once: (i) the code-selection cost of every RQ level, which is the Poincare distance rather than a Euclidean one, and (ii) the residual transport between consecutive levels, where the residual is defined, damped and re-exponentiated in the tangent space at the origin of the curved ball. Codebook updates use the Riemannian exp_0 retraction form.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of curvature c = 1 (fixed, scale-derived: encoder outputs are L2-normalized to radius 0.5 so that no point approaches the boundary at initialization), with geodesic distance d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u) (+) v||), log map log_0^c(z) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||z||) z/||z||, exp map exp_0^c(a) = tanh(sqrt(c)||a||/2) a/(sqrt(c)||a||), and Riemannian rescaling of codebook gradients.
ideas.key_change: The level-(l+1) input is no longer a plain residual; it is exp_0^c of a tangent residual whose component perpendicular to the successor direction g_x is scaled by (1-kappa_x), where kappa_x = |cos angle(u_l, g_x)| is measured per item; level-l code selection uses the curvature-c distance d_c(z_l, e_{l,k}) and codebook updates are Riemannian.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The successor table is built exclusively from the training split that Stage 2 also sees; validation and test interactions are never read by the SID construction, and the epoch-1500 refresh also reads only the training split. The Stage-3 evaluation split is used only after SIDs are frozen, exactly as in the frozen protocol. No test/validation transition, co-occurrence or popularity statistic enters g_x, kappa_x or the codebook.
ideas.motivation: An RQ-VAE spends its deep prefixes on idiosyncratic reconstruction detail that no history can predict, so the Stage-3 generator must guess level-2/3 tokens that carry no transferable meaning. If the residual handed from level l to level l+1 were stripped of the components that contradict what items of this kind actually transition to, the deep prefixes would encode behaviourally predictable distinctions and the generative model would land on the true SID more often.
ideas.novelty: Prior work here touched the codebook mean, the per-level curvature schedule, the radial rank of codes, target smoothing, cone constraints, boost shifts and curvature experts. This proposal touches none of those: it acts on the tangent-space residual that propagates between RQ levels, and it re-anisotropizes that residual with a per-item scalar kappa_x that is MEASURED from the angle between the residual and the training-only successor direction (no entropy, no radius rank, no codebook averaging, no extra parameters).
ideas.observables: (1) Stage-3 test_recall@10 (> 0.065 is the target). (2) History-conditioned hit rate of the level-2 and level-3 token: fraction of test targets whose greedy level-l prefix equals the target's level-l prefix, compared with the level-1 rate. (3) Per-level assignment entropy and dead-code count. (4) Fraction of items whose level-2/3 code differs from the code the Euclidean/behaviour-off geometry would give, from a frozen SID snapshot (diagnostic only, never a gate). (5) Mean measured kappa per level, which should be well away from 0 if the coupling is active.
risks: Tail items with few or noisy successors give kappa ~ 0 and the mechanism degenerates to the plain curved quantizer (no gain, no harm).; Suppressing the perpendicular residual may remove the capacity needed to separate confusable items, producing coarser prefixes.; Tangent-space residual subtraction in a Poincare ball can shrink residual magnitude and starve level-3 codes (dead codes).; The Stage-3 protocol may not be able to exploit better prefix predictability if generation is dominated by level-1.; A single run leaves seed noise inside the measured delta.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped to 1 - 1e-5, computed in log1p form for float32 stability; all ball points re-clipped to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c) after every exp map and every codebook step; kappa clamped to [0, 1 - 1e-6] and set to 0 when ||g_x|| < eps or ||u|| < eps (no-successor and degenerate-residual fallback); the residual update is provably non-expansive (||u_{l+1}||^2 = (1-kappa)^2 ||u_perp||^2 + ||u_par||^2 <= ||u||^2) so it cannot blow up; g_x normalized before use and items with fewer than two successor counts fall back to behaviour-off for that item; gradient clipping at the baseline value; straight-through estimator for the hard code index; the successor table is built once and refreshed only at the fixed epoch 1500, reading only the training split; dead-code re-initialization is left exactly as in the baseline so the comparison is not confounded; no ablation arm and no sweep is run.
ideas.spec_equations: Inputs: item target z = normalize_to_radius_0.5(Encoder(x)) in R^d, d = 32 or 64; codebooks E_l = {e_{l,k}} in B_c, k = 1..256, l = 1..3; successor table {g_x}. Constants: c = 1; R = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) * 0.5) (max tangent radius); eps = 1e-8; kappa clamp [0, 1 - 1e-6].   a_1 = log_0^c(z)   for l = 1..3:       z_l = exp_0^c(a_l)       d_{l,k} = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( min( sqrt(c) * || (-z_l) (+) e_{l,k} ||, 1 - 1e-5 ) )       k_l = argmin_k d_{l,k}    # straight-through: hard index, soft gradient through softmin over -d_{l,k}       u = a_l - log_0^c(e_{l,k_l})       if ||g_x|| > eps and ||u|| > eps:           g_hat = g_x / ||g_x||           kappa = min( |<u, g_hat>| / ||u|| , 1 - 1e-6 )           a_{l+1} = (1 - kappa) * u + kappa * <u, g_hat> * g_hat       else:           a_{l+1} = u       if ||a_{l+1}|| > R: a_{l+1} *= R / ||a_{l+1}||   Loss: standard RQ-VAE objective (reconstruction from the sum of decoded codes, commitment beta unchanged) with the reconstruction distance taken in the curved space: L_rec = d_c(z, exp_0^c(sum_l log_0^c(e_{l,k_l})))^2 plus the commitment term; an implementation may equivalently compare tangent coordinates, the assignment, residual and codebook stay as above.   Codebook step (Riemannian): gradient in tangent coordinates g_e = dL/d(log_0^c e); retraction e <- exp_0^c( log_0^c(e) - eta * g_e * ((1 - c||e||^2)/2)^2 ), e re-clipped to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c); eta is the baseline codebook learning rate (no new constant).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Takes the encoder output z in the Poincare ball, the three codebooks in the ball, and the precomputed per-item successor direction g_x. Returns the per-level code indices (k_1, k_2, k_3), i.e. the Semantic ID, the per-level tangent residuals for the loss, the measured kappa per item per level, and gradients for the encoder and the codebooks. No new learnable parameters and no change to the Stage-3 interface.

specification.text: For each item at level l: curved assignment k_l = argmin_k (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-z_l) (+) e_{l,k}||); tangent residual u_l = log_0^c(z_l) - log_0^c(e_{l,k_l}); successor direction g_x precomputed from training transitions; kappa_l = |<u_l, g_x/||g_x||>| / max(||u_l||, eps); residual update u_{l+1} = (1-kappa_l) u_l + kappa_l <u_l, g_hat> g_hat, then ball-clipped and exponentiated as the next level input. Fixed curvature c = 1 with encoder outputs L2-normalized to radius 0.5 (documented default, not tuned); L = 3 levels, K = 256 codes per level. Full pseudocode is in spec_equations.

ideas.title: Successor-Aligned Anisotropic Residual in a Poincare RQ-VAE (behaviour-direction damping of the inter-level residual)

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The tilt is removed, Ct_ik = d_c(exp^c_0(r_i), exp^c_0(C_l[k]))^2, so the plan is a purely geometric balanced OT assignment carrying no successor information; the BEH_OFF path runs the same Sinkhorn on the same codebooks and the same constants. Implemented and correct, not trained this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The default and only trained run: c from the initial-encoder residual median, sigma^2 from the median nearest-codeword Poincare distance after k-means init, P from Stage-2 training transitions, running-average plans with one uniform warm-up epoch, 20 Sinkhorn iterations, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards at 24 steps per epoch, then the frozen Stage 3 protocol. No sweep, no seed repetition, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c is set to 0, so exp^c_0 is the identity and d_c becomes the Euclidean distance; Ct_ik = ||r_i - C_l[k]||^2 - sigma^2*log A_ik and the plan is a flat behaviour-tilted balanced assignment. The GEO_OFF path runs through the same functions with the manifold calls skipped. Implemented and correct, not trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: Scan the Stage-2 training split sequences only; count directed co-occurrences C_ij of item i followed by item j within a window of 2; set C_ii = 0; keep the 50 largest counts per row; row-normalize to P. At each training step, the level-l plan is accumulated into the detached running average m (24556 x K per level), and A_ik = sum_j P_ij m_jk + eps is the expected member mass of codeword k among item i's training successors.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transition prior from training sequences (row-normalized top-50 successor distribution per item, self-loops removed), converted into a successor-set overlap between an item and the current member set of each codeword.
ideas.cost_estimate: B ~ 1023 items per step (24556/24). Cost matrix 1023x256x32 per level ~ 8.4M MAC; 20 Sinkhorn iterations ~ 5.2M MAC per level; successor tilt sparse gather 1023x50x256 ~ 13M MAC per level; about 1.1e8 MAC per step, roughly 5-7 percent of step time, plus ~100 MB host memory for the four 24556x256 running-average plans (fp32). Estimated 1.5 extra hours over the 72000-step, 3000-epoch Stage 2 run on four cards; zero extra Stage 3 cost because vocabulary, sequence length and prefix trie are unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: Pplan = Sinkhorn_20( exp( -( d_{P,c}( exp^c_0(r_i), exp^c_0(C_l[k]) )^2 - sigma^2 * log( sum_j P_ij m_jk + eps ) ) / sigma^2 ) ), and k_l = argmax_k Pplan_ik.
ideas.coupling_path: residual r_i -> exp^c_0 -> Poincare distance to exp^c_0(C_l[k]) -> cost matrix -> Sinkhorn plan under a usage-balance constraint -> row argmax gives token k_l -> that token drives the baseline quantization and commitment losses and the next residual. The behaviour log-prior enters the same cost matrix, and the plan is literally exp(-d_Poincare^2/sigma^2) multiplied by A_ik, so zeroing A_ik (behaviour off) or setting c = 0 (geometry off) each changes the plan, hence the token, hence the gradient that shapes the whole prefix hierarchy.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the token-choice operator rather than the codebook contents is the binding constraint on prefix quality, then the coupled run should show higher training-transition prefix adjacency and higher level-wise usage entropy than the recorded baseline while keeping reconstruction distortion within 3 percent of baseline, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 should clear 0.065. If recall is flat while adjacency and usage entropy rise, the assignment change is not what the generator needs; if recall falls while prefix mass concentrates, the successor tilt is collapsing level-1 discriminability.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ quantizer, at the assignment step of every level; codebook contents, codebook updates, the residual chain, the reconstruction and the decoder are untouched.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature -c with c = 1/(4*median||r_1||^2); exponential map exp^c_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)/(sqrt(c)||v||) * v; distance d_c(x,q) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x) (+) q||) with Mobius addition (+). The squared Poincare distance is the transport cost, and its Riemannian scale, not a tuned constant, sets the entropic temperature.
ideas.key_change: At every level the current Euclidean residual and every codeword are mapped into the Poincare ball of curvature -c; a cost matrix d_Poincare^2 minus sigma^2*log(item-to-codeword-member successor overlap) is turned into a doubly-stochastic plan by 20 log-domain Sinkhorn iterations, and the SID token becomes the argmax of that plan instead of the argmin of the Euclidean distance. Reconstruction, decoder, token vocabulary, sequence length and the Stage 3 pipeline are byte-identical to baseline.
ideas.leakage_boundary: P, m, c and sigma^2 are built only from Stage-2 training sequences and training forward passes. No validation or test interaction enters the transition counts, the plans, the codebooks, the curvature or the temperature. The item-to-token table is produced by the same procedure as the baseline, from training items only, with the identical vocabulary size, so Stage 3 sees exactly the information it saw before; behavioural diagnostics are computed on training transitions, never on validation or test pairs.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE SIDs are built by a per-item nearest-neighbour argmin in a flat tangent space. Nothing in that rule knows that item i is usually followed by item j, and nothing in it allocates codeword capacity to the items the generator must actually emit; the resulting prefix hierarchy is neither behaviourally coherent nor usage-balanced, which makes prefix-level generation for next-item recommendation harder than it must be. The problem addressed is that the assignment operator itself, not the codebook contents, decides whether a prefix means anything to the sequence model.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms in this programme changed codebook means (successor-weighted Frechet/Karcher), set the curvature value from a prefix-transition score, ranked items radially by behaviour entropy, built behaviour cones, smoothed Lorentz successor profiles, shifted prefixes behaviourally, mixed curvature per branch, used a token-side graph, or transported a behaviour vector along the residual chain. None of them replaced the assignment operator. This idea leaves codebook contents, the curvature value, the radii and the residual chain exactly as in the baseline and changes only how a codeword is selected at each level: the per-item argmin becomes one batch entropic optimal-transport plan whose cost is a Poincare distance (geometry) minus a successor-overlap log prior (behaviour), constrained by usage balance. The SID token is the row argmax of that plan, so the whole prefix hierarchy is the output of a transport problem that neither the behaviour term nor the curvature term can produce alone.
ideas.observables: Training-transition prefix adjacency (fraction of consecutive training pairs sharing the first token, and sharing the first two tokens); mean row entropy of the plan and its drift over epochs; level-wise token usage entropy and Gini; correlation between token mass and item demand; reconstruction distortion relative to baseline; the plan's total transport cost per epoch; Stage 3 test_recall@10 as the only judgement.
risks: Batch-level plans make token assignments mildly batch-composition dependent, so token noise between steps may dominate a single-run verdict.; The successor tilt can pull many items onto codewords whose members are popular successors, destroying level-1 discriminability (high adjacency, worse recall).; The balanced usage marginal fights the reconstruction objective on skewed item popularity, raising distortion for head items.; The Poincare cost can be nearly rank-equivalent to the Euclidean cost if codeword norms stay uniform, making the geometry arm almost identical and the coupling nominally present but inert.; The detached running-average plan can lag behind moving codebooks and feed stale successor statistics.; Top-50 successor rows miss long-tail items, which fall back to the pure curved cost and concentrate any gain in head items.; A single run with no ablation means the judgement rests on one recall number; behavioural diagnostics cannot rescue it.
ideas.safeguards: Log-domain Sinkhorn with 1e-8 added to G, fixed 20 iterations, row and column renormalisation after each half-step; clip sqrt(c)||r|| and sqrt(c)||C_l[k]|| to at most 1.0 so the Poincare radius stays at or below tanh(1) ~ 0.76 and the metric factor cannot blow up; clamp the Mobius sum norm to 1-1e-6 before artanh and use a Taylor branch of artanh for arguments below 1e-4; add 1e-8 to every norm before division; empty successor rows give S_ik = 1e-8 only, so those items are assigned by the pure curved cost; deterministic tie-breaking on the lowest codebook index; m is a detached buffer, warm-started at uniform 1/K for one epoch, never receives gradient and never leaves the training split; c and sigma^2 are frozen after measurement so no constant drifts into a tuned value; codebooks, vocabulary size, sequence length and prefix trie stay identical to baseline, and SID collisions are handled exactly as before, so Stage 3 and its feeding code need no modification.
ideas.spec_equations: c = 1/(4*median_i||r_{1,i}||^2); sigma^2 = median_i min_k d_c(exp^c_0(r_{1,i}), exp^c_0(C_1[k]))^2; C_ij = sum over training sequences of 1[j follows i within window 2], C_ii = 0, P = rownorm(keeptop50(C)). For level l = 1..L: x = exp^c_0(r); q_k = exp^c_0(C_l[k]); S_ik = sum_j P_ij m_jk + 1e-8; Ct_ik = d_c(x,q_k)^2 - sigma^2*log S_ik; G_ik = exp(-Ct_ik/sigma^2); log-domain Sinkhorn 20 iterations alternating row scaling to 1/B and column scaling to 1/K; k_l = argmax_k Pplan_ik; m <- (t*m + batchmean(Pplan))/(t+1) with m detached; residual update, reconstruction and losses identical to the baseline RQ-VAE with C_l[k_l] and a straight-through estimator.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: latent z and its per-level Euclidean residual r (d=32), codebooks C_l (K x d per level, L=4), sparse P (24556 x 24556, 50 per row), running-average plans m_l (24556 x K, detached), and the two measured constants c and sigma^2. Outputs: the SID token tuple (k_1..k_L), the plan Pplan of every level for diagnostics and for the m update, and the unchanged quantization and commitment losses with their unchanged weights.

specification.text: Per level l with Euclidean residual r_i in R^d: x_i = exp^c_0(r_i), q_k = exp^c_0(C_l[k]); A_ik = sum_j P_ij m_jk + eps with P the row-normalized top-50 training transition matrix and m the detached running-average plan of level l, eps = 1e-8; Ct_ik = d_c(x_i,q_k)^2 - sigma^2*log A_ik; G = exp(-Ct/sigma^2); 20 log-domain Sinkhorn iterations u = 1/(G v), v = 1/(G^T u) with marginals 1/B and 1/K; Pplan = diag(u) G diag(v); token k_l = argmax_k Pplan_ik; the baseline quantization and commitment losses are then applied to C_l[k_l] with a straight-through estimator exactly as before, so no new loss weight appears. Constants are measured, not chosen: c = 1/(4*median_i||r_{1,i}||^2) from the frozen initial encoder over the 24556 training items, sigma^2 = median_i min_k d_c(exp^c_0(r_{1,i}), exp^c_0(C_1[k]))^2 after k-means codebook init, m a plain cumulative average (no rate constant), 20 Sinkhorn iterations as the documented default.

ideas.title: Behaviour-tilted hyperbolic optimal-transport assignment: a Sinkhorn plan over a Poincare cost, tilted by a training-only successor-set prior, chooses every RQ-SID token

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The switch exists as lambda_i=0 for every item, so m_i=phi(r_i) and the run is the same Lorentzian RQ assignment without transition guidance. It is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: lambda_i from P, b_i from the stop-gradient residual bank, geodesic transport, and Lorentzian code scoring. This is the single candidate trained once on the frozen budget.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The switch exists as m_E=(1-lambda_i) r_i + lambda_i b_i and score_ik=-||m_E-c_lk||^2, keeping the transition term but replacing all exp/log/Lorentz distance by Euclidean computation. It is not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From Stage2 train split only: count C_ij over consecutive pairs (i,j), i != j; P_ij=C_ij/sum_j C_ij; m_i=number of nonzero successors; H_i=-sum_j P_ij log P_ij; lambda_i=0 if m_i=0, 1 if m_i=1, else max(0,1-H_i/log m_i) times a Laplace trust C_i/(C_i+1) with C_i=sum_j C_ij. Keep at most the K=256 highest-count successors per row. The residual bank is updated only from training-batch items.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions u_t -> u_{t+1} from the Stage2 training sequences, summarized as a row-normalised successor distribution P_i and a concentration weight lambda_i.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time O(T) transition counting with T Stage2 training transitions; memory sparse P plus an N x L x d float32 residual bank, about 18 MB for N=24556, L=3, d=64. Per step O(L B (D d + K d)) against baseline O(L B K d), with D capped at K=256. At the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs), expected quantizer overhead about 8-15% and wall-clock 1.1-1.2x baseline; the extra encoder work is zero because b_i reuses stored stop-gradient residuals.
ideas.coupling_equation: m_i^(l) = exp_{phi(r_i^(l))}( lambda_i(P_i) * log_{phi(r_i^(l))}( phi( b_i^(l)(P_i) ) ) );  score_ik = - d_L( m_i^(l), phi(c_lk) );  b_i^(l) = sum_j P_ij R_l[j] / max(sum_j P_ij, eps).
ideas.coupling_path: P -> (lambda_i, b_i) -> geodesic m_i -> Lorentz distance to codebook -> selected RQ prefix code. Removing behaviour sets lambda_i=0 so m_i=phi(r_i); removing curvature replaces the geodesic and Lorentz distance by Euclidean interpolation and squared distance. Both changes alter the same code-selection computation.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If directed transitions carry prefix-level information that reconstruction misses, the coupled run should assign prefixes that are more predictable from training transitions and should raise Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. The idea is rejected if recall stays at or below the baseline despite a measured increase in prefix-transition predictability, or if the coupled assignment collapses code usage without a recall gain.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, at every residual level l, after the encoder produces r_i^(l) and before the code lookup; the same curved metric scores all codebook entries for that level.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz model with fixed negative curvature -1: phi(v)=(sqrt(1+||v||^2),v); Minkowski inner product <x,y>_L=-x0 y0 + x.y; d_L(x,y)=arcosh(-<x,y>_L); geodesic exp_p and log_p on the hyperboloid, plus the Lorentz distance used as the code-assignment score.
ideas.key_change: At each RQ level replace the Euclidean nearest-code query r_i by a geodesic point m_i = exp_{phi(r_i)}(lambda_i log_{phi(r_i)}(phi(b_i))), where b_i is the directed-transition-weighted mean of successor residuals and lambda_i is the measured transition concentration; score codes by -d_L(m_i, phi(c_lk)).
ideas.leakage_boundary: P, lambda and the residual bank are built exclusively from Stage2 training sequences and training-batch encoder outputs. Validation and test interactions are never read, counted, or used to update P, lambda or the bank; Stage3 only consumes the frozen SID table produced after Stage2. No user or item from validation/test enters the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built from content reconstruction alone; a prefix that is easy to reconstruct can still be a poor predictor of the next item. Directed training transitions contain prefix-level successor structure that the quantizer never sees.
ideas.novelty: Unlike successor-Fréchet codebook updates, radial behaviour ranking, or per-level curvature control, this mechanism leaves the codebook update intact and changes the quantizer input/query: every RQ level transports the residual point along a hyperbolic geodesic toward a stop-gradient transition-weighted successor barycenter, then assigns the code by Lorentzian distance. Behaviour and curvature meet inside the same assignment equation.
ideas.observables: SID prefix assignments and prefix counts; training-split prefix-transition log-likelihood (predicting next item's prefix from current item's prefix under P); fraction of items whose selected prefix changes under behaviour-on; code usage entropy; mean geodesic displacement lambda_i d(phi(r_i),phi(b_i)); Stage3 test Recall@10.
risks: Residual bank staleness makes b_i noisy, especially for long-tail items.; For deterministic transitions lambda_i approaches 1 and the query can become the successor barycenter, collapsing distinct predecessors to one prefix.; Sparse or popularity-dominated transitions encode mostly popular successors and hurt tail items.; Lorentz distances saturate for large residual norms, reducing assignment margin.; The hyperbolic query increases reconstruction error because the selected code need not approximate r_i.; Additional gather/scatter over P and the bank may cost more than estimated if the transition graph is dense.; Single-run seed noise can swamp a small recall gain.
ideas.safeguards: Clip alpha to >=1+eps before arcosh; clip all residual, bank and code norms to 1e4; if d<eps or sinh(d)<eps set m_i=p; if Z_i<eps or lambda_i=0 set behaviour term to zero; cap transition row to K=256 entries; keep lambda_i in [0,1]; use float64 for alpha and arcosh or a stable arcosh(x)=log(x+sqrt(x^2-1)); replace any non-finite m_i or logit with the Euclidean fallback for that item; validate with torch.isfinite before the backward pass.
ideas.spec_equations: 1) Build P: C_ij=sum_t 1[u_t=i,u_{t+1}=j], i!=j; P_ij=C_ij/sum_j C_ij; m_i=|{j:C_ij>0}|; H_i=-sum_j P_ij log P_ij; lambda_i = 0 if m_i=0; 1 if m_i=1; else max(0,1-H_i/log m_i) * C_i/(C_i+1), C_i=sum_j C_ij. Cap each row to at most K=256 largest C_ij. 2) Bank: for each level l keep R_l in R^{N x d} and mask M_l; initialise 0. At a training step use the previous values; after the forward pass set R_l[i]=sg(r_i^(l)), M_l[i]=1 for batch items i. 3) Query: w_ij=P_ij M_l[j], Z_i=sum_j w_ij; b_i=sum_j w_ij R_l[j]/max(Z_i,eps); if Z_i<eps or lambda_i=0 set m_i=phi(r_i). Else p=phi(r_i), q=phi(b_i), alpha=-<p,q>_L, alpha=max(alpha,1+eps), d=arcosh(alpha), u=(q-cosh(d)p)/sinh(d), m_i=cosh(lambda_i d)p + sinh(lambda_i d)u. 4) Assign: z_ik=-d_L(m_i,phi(c_lk))=-arcosh(max(1+eps, m_i0 sqrt(1+||c_lk||^2)-m_i.spatial . c_lk)); k*=argmax_k z_ik; forward code c_lk*, straight-through gradient to m_i; r_i^(l+1)=r_i^(l)-c_lk*. Keep the baseline commitment, reconstruction and codebook updates unchanged.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training sequences, item count N, encoder residual r_i^(l) for batch items at each level, codebooks c_l, fixed K=256, fixed curvature -1, epsilon. Outputs: a selected code k* at every level for every item, hence the SID tuple, plus the stop-gradient residual bank used on later steps; also the assignment logits for diagnostics.

specification.text: Precompute a sparse row-normalised directed transition matrix P from Stage2 training sequences only. At each level l keep a stop-gradient residual bank R_l. For each batch item compute b_i from P and the bank, set lambda_i from the entropy of P_i, form the Lorentz geodesic point m_i between phi(r_i) and phi(b_i), and choose the code minimising Lorentz distance from m_i to phi(c_lk). Residual update and baseline RQ-VAE losses are otherwise unchanged. Switches: behaviour-off sets lambda_i=0; geometry-off replaces exp/log/d_L by Euclidean linear interpolation and squared distance.

ideas.title: Behaviour-directed Lorentzian geodesic residual assignment for RQ-VAE semantic IDs

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: lambda_i set to 0 for every item, so p~_l = p_l and the pipeline reduces to a fixed-curvature hyperbolic RQ with Sinkhorn assignment; the switch exists in code (a boolean that zeroes the behaviour tensor) and is correct but is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: derived lambda_i, Lorentzian successor barycenter from the tangent cache, geodesic interpolation at the live query point, squared Poincare cost, Sinkhorn with uniform column marginal, Moebius residual recursion. This is the single trained candidate of the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp/log/Moebius/d_P/Lorentz centroid replaced by identity maps, the weighted Euclidean successor mean and squared L2 cost, keeping lambda_i, the Sinkhorn structure, the residuals and all constants identical; one flag selects the Euclidean branch and it is exercised only by unit tests, not by a training arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: Single pass over the TRAINING split sequences only: for each consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) with a gap of at most 1 within a session, increment C[i,j]. Then P(i->.) = C[i,:] / (sum_j C[i,j] + eps) (no popularity normalisation, no test data, no validation data), keep the top-M = 8 successors after a fixed, deterministic tie-break by item id, and store lambda_i = max_j P(i->j) with lambda_i = 0 when the outgoing count is zero. The tensor is frozen before Stage 2 starts and is never recomputed from any other split.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed training-only item-to-item transitions, reduced to two per-item quantities: the normalised successor distribution P(i->j) over the item's top-M successors, and its commitment lambda_i = max_j P(i->j).
ideas.cost_estimate: About +35-50% wall clock on the Stage 2 quantizer path, well under a full epoch of extra work. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, batch B ~ 1023, L = 4 levels, K = configured codebook size per level, say 256): 4 level loops, each with B*M = 1023*8 = 8184 cache gathers, one closed-form Lorentz centroid (8184 x 33 add-multiply), one B*K = 262k squared Poincare distance matrix (a few 1e6 FLOPs) and 30 Sinkhorn iterations over a 1023x256 matrix (~30*262k*2 = 1.6e7 FLOPs); total ~7e7 extra FLOPs per step and ~5e12 over 3000 epochs (72k steps), which is small beside the transformer encoder. Extra memory: one tangent cache of 24556 x L x d floats (12.6 MB at d = 32) plus the read-only successor index (24556 x 8 ints, 0.8 MB). No extra backward pass, no extra forward of the encoder.
ideas.coupling_equation: p~_l[i] = exp_{p_l[i]}( lambda_i^(l) * log_{p_l[i]}( g_l[i] ) ),  lambda_i^(l) = max_j P(i->j) * ||log_0(p_l[i])|| / (||log_0(p_1[i])|| + 1e-8),  g_l[i] = pi_P( sum_j w_ij x_j^l / sqrt(|<sum_j w_ij x_j^l, sum_j w_ij x_j^l>_eta|) ),  then T = Sinkhorn( exp( -d_P(p~_l[i], c_l[k])^2 / eps ) ; 1/B, 1/K ) and k_l[i] = argmax_k T[i,k].
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour tensor -> lambda_i and successor set -> Lorentz barycenter g_l[i] of the cached successor points -> geodesic shift p~_l[i] = exp_{p_l}(lambda_i^(l) * log_{p_l}(g_l[i])) -> Poincare cost matrix M[i,k] -> Sinkhorn plan T -> code k_l[i] -> residual p_{l+1}[i]. Removing the behaviour sets lambda_i = 0 so p~ = p, which changes every cost entry, every plan and every code; removing the curvature replaces the barycenter, the interpolation and the cost by their Euclidean counterparts, which changes the same tensor. Both switches therefore act on one tensor, not on two independent losses.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behaviour-guided curved assignment targets are real, then in the single both-on run (i) per-level code usage entropy rises and stays high (uniform column marginal plus successor pulling prevents collapse), (ii) the fraction of training successor pairs that share the level-1 prefix rises materially over what an unshifted Euclidean RQ gives, (iii) a prefix-only next-item predictor computed on held-out training transitions from the frozen Stage 3 generator scores higher top-10 hit rate, and (iv) Stage 3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. If recall stays at or below 0.065 while usage entropy and successor prefix sharing do rise, the hypothesis that behaviour-guided curved assignment is the binding constraint is falsified for this budget.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, at every one of the L residual-quantisation levels: it defines the behaviour target (Lorentz centroid), the geodesic interpolation of the live query point, the Sinkhorn cost (squared Poincare distance), and the residual recursion (log_0 of the Moebius residual). It acts during Stage 2 training only; Stage 3 sees only the resulting integer SIDs.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature K = -1 on the Poincare ball (exp_0, log_0, log_p, Moebius subtraction, Poincare distance d_P) together with the closed-form weighted Lorentzian centroid on the hyperboloid of the same curvature (ambient weighted mean followed by re-projection onto the hyperboloid). Curvature is fixed, not tuned; only the point positions move.
ideas.key_change: At every RQ level the query point is first geodesically interpolated, by a per-item factor derived from its training successor distribution and the level's residual scale, toward the Lorentz-model weighted barycenter of that item's training successors; the resulting point is matched to codewords by a Sinkhorn-transported soft assignment whose cost is the squared Poincare distance with a measured (not swept) entropic scale and a uniform column marginal.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The behaviour tensor is built exclusively from sequences of the training split that Stage 2 already uses; validation and test interactions are never read by the SID construction path. lambda_i and P(i->.) are frozen file artefacts computed once before training, so no target item of a Stage 3 evaluation episode can influence any code assignment, the codebook, the curvature, or the tangent cache. The tangent cache is written only from encoder outputs on Stage 2 training batches, and Stage 3 evaluation is read-only with respect to it.
ideas.motivation: A generative recommender learns to emit SID prefixes; it only generalises to a target item if that item's coarse prefix is a region the prefix generator already visits after the user's history. Plain Euclidean RQ-VAE assigns codes from item identity alone, so two items that are behaviourally interchangeable (one reliably follows the other) can receive unrelated roots and the generator must memorise each transition separately. The fix is to make the quantizer's ASSIGNMENT TARGET, not merely its codebook, depend on where the item's training-successors already sit, and to make that target a curved object so that pulling an item toward a bundle of successors follows the true geometry of the latent rather than a chord through the ball.
ideas.novelty: Different coupling position from the discarded rounds: not curved codebook updates (Fréchet successor codebooks), not per-level curvature control (CURVCTRL-SID), not radial behaviour ranking of codes (BRad-RQ), not entailment cones over prefixes, not Lorentz profile smoothing, not geodesic residual booster. Here the behaviour signal defines a per-item DESTINATION in the manifold and the geometry defines both that destination (closed-form Lorentzian weighted centroid of the cached successor points) and the transport used to choose the code (Poincare cost matrix plus Sinkhorn with a uniform column marginal). Nothing is added as a side loss; the behaviour and the curvature meet inside the single assignment cost matrix, and the residual recursion continues from the resulting curved codeword, so both switches bite the same tensor.
ideas.observables: SID assignment: per-level code histograms, usage entropy and collision counts of the frozen SID table; gradient/parameter update: encoder norms and codebook EMA drift per level, plus the mean shift magnitude ||lambda_i^(l) log_{p_l}(g_l)|| tracked per epoch; prefix behaviour predictability: top-10 hit rate of a prefix-only successor predictor on held-out training transitions and the fraction of training successor pairs sharing level-1 and level-1-2 prefixes; Stage 3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 bar. All diagnostics are recorded, none gates the run.
risks: Successor pulling collapses many behaviourally overlapping items onto the same coarse prefix, so the generator cannot tell them apart and top-10 recall drops even though prefix predictability rises.; The tangent cache lags (momentum 0.9) while the encoder moves fast in early epochs, so the Lorentz barycenters are stale targets and inject noise.; Sinkhorn with a uniform column marginal may over-smooth: with B ~ 1023 rows and K columns the plan spreads mass across codes and argmax becomes unstable early in training.; Entropic scale eps = mean(M) is scale-relative but not curvature-relative; if the learned point cloud shrinks toward the origin, eps shrinks and the plan hardens abruptly.; Items with sparse training transitions get lambda_i near 0, so the mechanism only acts on the head of the transition graph and may not generalise to the long tail that dominates test recall.; Extra per-step cost on the quantizer path may force shorter effective training within the frozen 3000-epoch budget if wall-clock is capped.
ideas.safeguards: All exp/log maps use the clamped norm min(max(||.||, 1e-12), 1 - 1e-3) and 2*arctanh is evaluated as log((1+r)/(1-r)) for stability; the Lorentz re-projection uses |eta(xbar,xbar)| with a 1e-12 floor so a null or negative norm cannot produce NaN; the barycenter is fully detached (stop-grad) so no second-order graph runs through the cache; the entropic scale is the measured batch mean cost clipped to [1e-3, 1e2], and both Sinkhorn marginals are floors (1/B, 1/K) with 30 log-domain iterations so no division by zero occurs; empty code rows keep their previous values through Laplace smoothing 1e-5; items with no outgoing training transition and all items on the first step fall back exactly to the unshifted hyperbolic assignment so the mechanism can never make the objective ill-defined; a skipping rule never updates the cache from a batch containing a NaN loss; gradient clipping (repository default) applies to the straight-through assignment; no constant is swept: lambda_i comes from counts, the level strength from the residual-norm ratio, eps from the measured cost, the column marginal from 1/K, and the cache momentum 0.9, Sinkhorn iterations 30, M = 8 and K_c = -1 are documented defaults fixed before the run.
ideas.spec_equations: Notation: B batch, K codes/level, L levels, M = 8 successors, ball radius bound 1 - 1e-3, curvature K_c = -1. 1. p_1 = exp_0(z) = tanh(||z||) * z/max(||z||, 1e-12); clamp ||p_1|| <= 1 - 1e-3. 2. Cache: cache[i, l, :] is tangent-at-origin log_0(p_l[i]) written with momentum: cache <- 0.9*cache + 0.1*detach(log_0(p_l)). 3. Barycenter: v_j = cache[j, l, :]; x_j = [sqrt(1 + ||v_j||^2), v_j] in R^{d+1}; w_ij = P(i->j)/sum_{j in TopM(i)} P(i->j); xbar = sum_j w_ij x_j; s = |<xbar, xbar>_eta| with eta = diag(-1, 1, ..., 1); xg = xbar / sqrt(max(s, 1e-12)); g = xg[1:] / (xg[0] + 1) (Poincare ball). If ItemHasNoSuccessor(i): g = p_l[i], lambda_i = 0. 4. Derived strength: lambda_i^(l) = lambda_i * ||log_0(p_l[i])|| / (||log_0(p_1[i])|| + 1e-8). 5. Shift: p~ = exp_{p}(lambda^(l) * log_p(g)), log_p(g) = 2 arctanh(||(-p (+) g)||) * (-p (+) g)/||(-p (+) g)||, exp_p(u) = p (+) (tanh(||u||/2) * u/||u||). Clamp ||p~|| <= 1 - 1e-3. 6. Cost: M[i,k] = (2 arctanh(||(-p~_i) (+) c_l[k]||))^2; eps = clip(mean(M), 1e-3, 1e2); Kmat = exp(-M / eps). 7. Sinkhorn (log domain, 30 iterations): f = 0, gv = 0; repeat: f = -eps * logsumexp_k( (-M[i,k] + gv[k]) / eps ) + eps*log(1/B); gv = -eps * logsumexp_i( (-M[i,k] + f[i]) / eps ) + eps*log(1/K). Plan T = exp( (-M + f[:,None] + gv[None,:]) / eps ). 8. Assignment: A = T / T.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True); hard = onehot(argmax_k A); soft = A; q = hard + soft - soft.detach() (straight-through). Code index k_l[i] = argmax_k A[i,k]. 9. Codebook: EMA update with counts = q.sum(dim=0).detach(), decay 0.99, Laplace smoothing 1e-5. 10. Residual: t = log_0(p_l (-) c_l[k_l]); p_{l+1} = exp_0(t). Loop l = 1..L. 11. Loss: standard RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment (beta from the repository default); the mechanism adds no loss term, only the assignment path. 12. Switches: behaviour-off sets lambda_i = 0; geometry-off replaces arctanh distances by ||.||^2 and step 3 by the Euclidean weighted mean of cache[j, l, :], and steps 1/5/10 by identity maps.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z in R^{B x d} for the batch; the frozen behaviour artefact (top-M successor indices and probabilities per item, lambda_i per item); the frozen tangent cache of size N x L x d; the current per-level codebooks c_l in R^{K x d}. Outputs: per-level hard code indices k_l in {0..K-1}^B (concatenated into the item's SID tuple), the straight-through soft assignment q for the encoder backward pass and codebook EMA, the updated tangent cache rows for the batch, and diagnostics (usage counts, mean shift magnitude, mean Poincare cost) for the progress log.

specification.text: Encoder gives z (Euclidean). p_1 = exp_0(z) = tanh(||z||) * z/||z|| on the Poincare ball of curvature K=-1. For level l = 1..L: (1) fetch cached tangent-at-origin vectors of the top-M training successors of each batch item, map them to the hyperboloid, take the closed-form weighted Lorentzian centroid, project back to the ball to get g_l[i]; (2) shift the live query point p_l[i] geodesically toward g_l[i] by the derived fraction lambda_i^(l) = lambda_i * ||log_0(p_l[i])|| / (||log_0(p_1[i])|| + 1e-8), with lambda_i = max_j P(i->j) the item's top-1 training successor probability (0 if the item has no outgoing training transition); (3) build M[i,k] = d_P(p~_l[i], c_l[k])^2, entropic scale eps = mean(M) clipped to [1e-3, 1e2]; (4) run 30 log-domain Sinkhorn iterations with row marginal 1/B and column marginal 1/K to get plan T; take code k_l[i] = argmax_k T[i,k] with straight-through soft assignment T*K in the backward pass; (5) update the codebook by EMA on the detached soft counts; (6) residual tangent t = log_0(p_l[i] (-) c_l[k_l[i]]) (Moebius subtraction), p_{l+1}[i] = exp_0(t). Every step also writes p_l[i] into the tangent cache with momentum 0.9 (stop-grad). Loss = standard RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment; no extra loss term is introduced. Behaviour-off sets lambda_i = 0 (p~ = p, identical arithmetic); geometry-off replaces exp/log/d_P/the Lorentz centroid by identity maps, the weighted Euclidean mean and squared L2 (Sinkhorn structure unchanged); both-on is the full mechanism. One training run, no arm is trained off.

ideas.title: Behaviour-pulled curved assignment targets: geodesic interpolation toward the Lorentz barycenter of an item's successors, resolved by a Poincare-distance Sinkhorn plan inside the RQ-VAE

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Config use_behaviour=False: lam_i:=0 and s_l is never read, so x~_l = x_i and the run is a plain curved Mobius-composed RQ-VAE. The switch exists and is correct; no arm is trained with it in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single trained candidate: use_behaviour=True and use_hyperbolic=True, one seed, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep over lam, bound, temperature or any other constant, no extra arm.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Config use_hyperbolic=False: exp/log/Mobius/d_P replaced by identity, weighted mean and L2, giving x~_l = p_l + ||r_l||*normalize((1-lam_i)r_hat_l + lam_i*s_hat_l) and additive residual composition; behaviour survives as a flat blend, curvature disappears. The switch exists and is correct; no arm is trained with it.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: n_ij = number of times item j immediately follows item i across training sequences, w_ij=n_ij/sum_j n_ij, n_i=sum_j n_ij, nbar = median of n_i over items with n_i>0, all computed once before Stage 2 and frozen. The successor field at level l is s_l(i)=sum_j w_ij*log_{p_l(i)}(P_l[j]), where P_l is a detached buffer of each item's ball point (level 1) or prefix points (levels 2..L) written during Stage-2 training batches.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions from the training sequences, aggregated per item into a successor-prefix tangent field, plus the derived per-item reliability weight n_i/(n_i+nbar).
ideas.cost_estimate: Stage 2 only, at the frozen scale: 24556 training items / 24 steps = 1023 items per step. Per item per level the assignment evaluates 256 Mobius steps plus geodesic distances (~150 flops at D=32) = ~38k flops, so ~1.2e8 flops per step forward and the same backward, against ~2.5e7 flops for the baseline Euclidean assignment: about +1e8 flops per step, 7.2e10 per epoch, 2.2e14 over 3000 epochs, i.e. roughly +15-25% Stage-2 step time and under +2% end-to-end wall clock. Successor aggregation costs one index lookup and a degree-weighted 32-dim sum per item per level (<6k flops/item/level); the detached prefix buffer is N*L*D floats = 9.4 MB. Stage 3 unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: x~_l = exp_{p_l}( ||r_l|| * normalize( (1 - lam_i)*r_hat_l + lam_i*s_hat_l ) ), with r_l = log_{p_l}(x_i), s_l = sum_j w_ij * log_{p_l}(P_l[j]), lam_i = n_i/(n_i+nbar); k_l = argmin_k d_P^{c=-1}( p_{l-1} (+) u^l_k , x~_{l-1} ).
ideas.coupling_path: One connected pathway: encoder output -> ball point -> per-level prefix p_l -> tangent frame at p_l -> (successor prefix field at the same depth) rotated target x~ -> Mobius-step candidate points p_l(+)u^l_k -> geodesic distance coding choice k_l -> level-l prefix token -> prefix of level l+1. The behaviour signal enters only through the rotation of the target and the geometry only through exp/log/Mobius/d_P at p_l; with lam=0 the rotation is the identity (behaviour inert), with Euclidean exp/log/Mobius/d_P the rotation is a flat vector blend and the composition plain addition (curvature inert), so removing either changes the produced codes.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if (a) the mean derived coupling weight over items with training transitions does not collapse (report mean lam; if below 0.05 the run is declared behaviour-inert) and (b) the single frozen Stage 3 run reports test_recall@10 above 0.065 and above the programme baseline. The assignment must visibly change: level-2/3 token histograms and SID identity differ for high-lam items relative to what the behaviour-off configuration would produce, and prefix transition predictability at levels 2-3 rises while geodesic reconstruction error may rise slightly.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantization: in the forward pass that turns an item embedding into its L-token SID, once per level, and in the Stage-2 reconstruction and codebook losses; nothing is added to Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with fixed negative curvature c=-1: Mobius addition for the curved residual composition, geodesic distance d_P for assignment and reconstruction, and exp/log maps that define the tangent frame at each prefix point; code radius bound derived by equal geodesic budget d_max/L rather than chosen.
ideas.key_change: Before each RQ level the item residual direction log_p(x) is slerped toward the successor-prefix tangent field and the chosen code is the one whose Mobius step lands nearest that rotated target; the RQ-VAE therefore encodes transition-consistent residuals into the level-2 and level-3 tokens.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transitions, counts, nbar and the prefix buffer are computed exclusively from training-sequence interactions and from Stage-2 training batches; SIDs are built once and frozen before Stage 3. No validation or test sequence, interaction or score ever enters the counts, the buffer, the target rotation or the codebooks, so no information about held-out next items can reach the IDs.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are trained to reconstruct an item embedding, so level-2 and level-3 tokens spend their capacity on residual detail of the item itself and carry almost no information about which item the user consumes next; the generative recommender must then learn transition structure from the token sequence alone. Rotating the quantization target, level by level, toward where the item's successors sit in the prefix tree makes the whole prefix hierarchy behaviour-predictive instead of merely reconstructive.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms in this programme moved the codebook (successor-weighted Frechet centroid updates), changed curvature per level (measured prefix-transition score), or ranked items by radius (transition-entropy rank). This idea leaves codebooks, curvature (-1 fixed) and radii untouched and instead rotates the quantization TARGET direction inside the tangent frame of the current curved prefix, at constant geodesic radius, separately at every level, with a per-item coupling weight derived from transition counts, and composes the prefix path by Mobius addition so the hierarchy bends. It is an angular coupling, not a translational geodesic shift and not a centroid update.
ideas.observables: Mean and quartiles of lam; fraction of items with lam=0; per-level code-usage entropy; SID identity change rate relative to the behaviour-off configuration (assignment observable); geodesic reconstruction error; prefix transition predictability (fraction of test-sequence prefixes whose next token lies in the successor set of the prefix) recorded as a diagnostic only; frozen Stage 3 test_recall@10 as the sole judgement.
risks: The successor aggregate is coarse, so the rotated target can leave the item's own manifold and hurt reconstruction, hence token likelihood; Constraining all three code steps inside the ball radius cap limits expressivity of the last level; The detached successor prefix buffer is stale by up to one epoch and can oscillate or feed back into itself; Most items may have very few training transitions, driving lam toward 0 and making the run an ordinary curved RQ-VAE; Near-boundary Poincare arithmetic can blow up without clipping and projection; The Stage 3 generator may not exploit prefix coherence, in which case recall stays flat despite the coupling
ideas.safeguards: Clamp every ball norm to rho_max=0.9 before any Mobius operation and re-project to <=0.9 after each addition; epsilon 1e-8 in every denominator; clamp the atanh argument to 1-1e-6; a zero-radius code or zero residual skips exp/log and returns p unchanged; lam capped at 0.9 and forced to 0 when the successor field is missing (sparse-transition items, unstored buffer slots) so no item is dragged toward the origin by a phantom direction; the code-radius projection runs after the optimizer step, not inside the graph; the successor buffer is written with detached values only and never back-propagated; stale entries are refreshed lazily on appearance and unseen successors fall back to lam=0; loss is NaN-checked every 50 steps with a floor of 1e-6 on the Mobius denominator (no constant is changed); nothing derived is re-tuned if the mean lam turns out low - the run is reported as behaviour-inert.
ideas.spec_equations: c=1 (curvature -1). Ball embedding x = rho_max*z/(kappa+||z||), kappa = running RMS of ||z|| over the first 200 steps, rho_max=0.9. Derived code bound: d_max=2*atanh(rho_max); per level u^l_k <- u^l_k * min(1, tanh((d_max/L)/2)/max(||u^l_k||,1e-8)). Mobius: a(+)b = ((1+2<a,b>+||b||^2)a + (1-||a||^2)b)/(1+2<a,b>+||a||^2||b||^2). Distance: d_P(a,b)=2*atanh(min(||(-a)(+)b||, 1-1e-6)). log_p(x) = (2/lambda_p)*atanh(min(||(-p)(+)x||,1-1e-6))*((-p)(+)x)/||(-p)(+)x||, lambda_p=1-||p||^2. exp_p(v) = p (+) ( tanh(lambda_p*||v||/2)*v/||v|| ). Forward per item: p_0=0; for l=1..L: r=log_{p_{l-1}}(x); s=sum_j w_ij log_{p_{l-1}}(P_l[j]); lam=0 if ||s||<1e-6 else min(0.9, n_i/(n_i+nbar)); d_hat=normalize((1-lam)*r/max(||r||,1e-8) + lam*s/||s||); x~=exp_{p_{l-1}}(||r||*d_hat); k_l=argmin_k d_P(p_{l-1}(+)u^l_k, x~) with straight-through (hard index, soft gradient to the selected u); p_l=p_{l-1}(+)u^l_{k_l}; write p_l into detached buffer slot (i,l). Loss L = d_P(p_L,x)^2 + beta*mean_l d_P(p_{l-1}(+)u^l_{k_l}, sg[x~_l])^2 + geodesic codebook term, beta=0.25 default, straight-through estimator. SIDs=argmin indices per level, frozen, fed to the unchanged Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z in R^D, transition counts n_ij with derived w_ij and nbar, detached prefix buffer P in R^{N x L x D}, codebooks U^l in R^{K x D} inside the ball. Outputs: the L-token SID (k_1..k_L) per item, the geodesic reconstruction loss with gradients for encoder and codebooks, and the diagnostics (lam distribution, per-level usage entropy, geodesic error).

specification.text: Poincare ball of fixed curvature -1; rho_max=0.9; ball embedding x = rho_max*z/(kappa+||z||) with kappa the running RMS of ||z|| measured over the first 200 Stage-2 steps; code radius bound derived by equal geodesic budget d(0,u^l_k) <= d_max/L with d_max=2*atanh(rho_max), L=3, K=256; per level: r=log_{p}(x), s=sum_j w_ij*log_{p}(P_l[j]) with P_l the detached prefix buffer, lam_i=n_i/(n_i+nbar) capped at 0.9, target x~=exp_p(||r||*normalize((1-lam)r_hat+lam*s_hat)); assignment k_l=argmin_k d_P(p(+)u^l_k, x~); prefix p <- p(+)u^l_{k_l}; loss d_P(p_L,x)^2 + beta*commitment (beta=0.25) + geodesic codebook term, straight-through estimator; SIDs frozen and handed to the unchanged Stage 3 protocol.

ideas.title: Successor-prefix tangent-direction rotation of the quantization target inside a Poincare RQ-VAE: behaviour turns the residual direction at constant geodesic radius before every level

objective: Improve the item semantic IDs of a generative recommender: a training-only behaviour signal must guide the whole SID prefix hierarchy in a hyperbolic RQ-VAE, and the result must raise the Stage 3 test recall above 0.065.
